summary: De-render Slack's wire markup at the presentation boundary of the archive-backed commands, so message bodies reach output as readable text instead of raw <@U…>/<#C…>/<!here>/<https://…|label> spans and &/</> entities.
reason: Slack has no rendered-text field: conversations.history returns bodies in Slack's own encoding, and every command that prints a message body was passing it through verbatim. In a real workspace that is not an edge case — the sampled mirror's most common message is literally "<@U0EXAMPLE01> has joined the channel", and quoted-reply blocks arrive as "> …". Users and agents reading `text`, `parent_text`, or `last_reply_text` saw opaque IDs where a name belonged, and a truncated preview could strand half a span ("<@U0BK3A") in the output. The fix is one shared renderer (slackanalytics.TextRenderer) that resolves user and channel IDs against the local mirror, degrades unresolvable IDs to a readable @ID/#ID form, keeps link targets visible because a terminal cannot carry a hyperlink, and decodes entities through cliutil.CleanText. It runs only on the way out: the store keeps Slack's encoding so ClassifyMention and full-text search keep working against the form Slack actually sent, and `sql`/`export` stay fidelity-preserving.
validated_outcome: Verified against a live 991-message mirror, read-only. `archive recall` now emits "@GitHub has joined the channel" and "Run: https://github.com/…" where it previously emitted "<@U0EXAMPLE01> …" and "<https://github.com/…>"; `catchup` and `threads stale` previews render "@Codex can you read the plan above" and "> Begin now by inspecting…". A post-run store check confirms the 7 rows carrying raw <@ markup are unchanged. Table-driven tests cover every markup form, mirror-vs-inline-label precedence, unresolvable IDs, the zero-value renderer, multiple and adjacent spans in one body, unknown constructs (left visible rather than deleted), a byte-identical passthrough assertion for markup-free bodies including whitespace/multiline/unicode, and a regression guard asserting that rendered text no longer classifies as a mention — i.e. that callers classify before rendering.
upstream: Any API whose text fields carry a provider-specific markup dialect (Slack mrkdwn, Discord mentions, Jira wiki markup) hits this. The generator could accept a per-spec `text_rendering` declaration — a list of pattern → replacement rules plus the resource whose rows resolve embedded IDs — and emit the renderer plus its presentation-boundary wiring, instead of every such CLI hand-writing one. The narrower reusable half is a scaffold convention: novel commands that surface a provider text field should render at assignment time, never at scan time.
